name: Trigeminal sensory and motor nuclei
summary: The trigeminal nerve has the longest nuclear column in the brainstem. The principal (chief) sensory nucleus in the rostral pons receives discriminative touch from the face; the spinal nucleus below it receives pain and temperature; the mesencephalic nucleus above it is the only place where primary sensory cell bodies sit inside the central nervous system, serving jaw proprioception; and the motor nucleus, medial to the principal nucleus, drives the muscles of mastication. Together they let a single pontine lesion produce facial numbness with a weak jaw deviating toward the lesion.

anatomy.location: Principal sensory and motor nuclei: lateral tegmentum of the mid-pons at the level of the trigeminal root entry. Mesencephalic nucleus: a slender column along the lateral edge of the periaqueductal gray up to the superior colliculus. Spinal nucleus: descending through the medulla to C2–C3.

subdivisions.name: Principal sensory nucleus
subdivisions.note: fine touch and pressure from the face; projects in the trigeminal lemniscus, mostly crossed, to VPM

subdivisions.name: Motor nucleus
subdivisions.note: masseter, temporalis, pterygoids, mylohyoid, anterior digastric, tensor tympani, tensor veli palatini; bilateral corticobulbar input

subdivisions.name: Mesencephalic nucleus
subdivisions.note: proprioception from jaw muscles and periodontal ligament; afferent limb of the jaw jerk

subdivisions.name: Spinal nucleus
subdivisions.note: pain, temperature and crude touch (see the spinal trigeminal entry)

function: All facial somatic sensation, the sensory side of the corneal, blink and jaw-jerk reflexes, and motor control of chewing.

bestView.label: lateral mid-pontine tegmentum at the trigeminal root entry
root leaving the pons toward Meckel's cave

imaging.normalAppearance: The trigeminal root is a well-seen band on axial T2 crossing the prepontine cistern; the nuclei are not resolved. Pontine plaques at the root entry zone are a frequent cause of trigeminal symptoms in multiple sclerosis.

pathology.finding: FLAIR-bright lesion at the lateral pons where the root enters; trigeminal neuralgia or facial numbness.
Restricted diffusion in the lateral mid-pons with ipsilateral facial sensory loss and contralateral body sensory loss.
Dumbbell enhancing mass along the root and Meckel's cave.

imaging.sequenceOfChoice: Thin axial T2/FLAIR of the pons; CISS/FIESTA and T1+Gd for the root

lesionEffects.deficit: Jaw deviates toward the lesion on opening with masseter wasting
lesionEffects.mechanism: Motor nucleus or motor root: the intact lateral pterygoid pushes the jaw to the weak side

lesionEffects.deficit: Absent jaw jerk with an otherwise brisk reflex pattern

examination: Light touch and pin-prick in V1, V2, V3 on each side
Palpate the masseters while the patient clenches; watch jaw opening for deviation
pearls: Loss of touch but preserved pain on the face means the principal nucleus (pons), whereas the reverse means the spinal nucleus (medulla)
A brisk jaw jerk with a brisk everything else points to a lesion above the pons
